sources.summary: git patch-id defaults to UNSTABLE hash unless --stable is passed or patchid.stable=true. --stable is required for cross-environment/config determinism. patch-id ignores whitespace and line numbers; it is a symmetrical sum of SHA-1 over file diffs.

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment:
The core design is sound and correctly targets the real failure surface. Root cause is accurate: detectSquashMergeByTree and both ancestry checks (verifyChangeBranchReachable, verifyChangeBranchReachableFromOrigin) all dereference the live `change/{id}` ref, so a squash-merge followed by branch deletion leaves no structural proof on the retry path (verifyReleaseEvidenceFromMain), and the release gate stays pending. Persisting a trusted change-tip SHA into phase9_status and substituting it for the live ref in tree-SHA comparison is the minimal, correct structural fix. It preserves the shipped-invariant bar (still requires positive tree/patch/PR proof) and degrades gracefully for legacy in-flight changes (optional field, falls back to live-ref behavior). Reuse of the existing tree-SHA comparison via a single rev-parse substitution is a good LBP call and keeps existing tests green.

Gaps and corrections found:

1. TIP CAPTURE POINT / SUBJECT MISMATCH (medium). Design text says capture via `git -C {worktreePath} rev-parse change/{id}`. Two issues: (a) The capture must land in the FIRST recordPhase9Status({status:pending}) at change.ts:2580 (before finalizeRelease/dispatch), because the retry path is exactly when the worktree/branch is gone. If tip is only captured later it will be unavailable on retry. (b) `rev-parse change/{id}` and `rev-parse HEAD` in an ADV worktree that is checked out on change/{id} are equivalent, but HEAD is the more robust subject if the worktree is ever detached; either is acceptable given validateChangeWorktree already asserts the branch. More important: detectSquashMergeByTree computes the tree in mainCheckout, so the persisted SHA must be a commit object present in mainCheckout's object store (it is, since worktrees share the object DB), and the helper must switch to `rev-parse {tip}^{tree}` — confirm the tip commit is fetched/reachable in mainCheckout after branch deletion (shared .git object store makes this true unless GC pruned it; deletion alone does not prune).

2. PATCH-ID DETERMINISM (medium, must-fix). git patch-id defaults to the UNSTABLE hash unless `--stable` is passed or patchid.stable=true is configured (git-scm docs). The design's `git diff {base}..{tip} | git patch-id` is non-deterministic across environments/config and will silently mismatch. detectSquashMergeByPatchId MUST use `git patch-id --stable` on BOTH sides (change diff and each trunk commit's `git show --stable`-equivalent via `git diff-tree -p | git patch-id --stable`). Also the design's `git show {commit} | git patch-id` for merge commits emits combined diffs that patch-id skips; use `git diff-tree -p --no-merges` piping to be safe.

3. SCHEMA REGEN IS MANDATORY, NOT CONDITIONAL (low, must-fix in planning). Phase9FinalizationStatusSchema is embedded in ChangeSchema which IS a public registry entry (schema-registry.ts:32) and in the Temporal Phase9StatusUpdatedSignalPayload. Adding an optional field requires `pnpm run schemas:generate` and will be caught by `pnpm run schemas:check` in CI. The design hedges ('if it is in the registry ... confirm during planning') — it definitively is. Make it a firm planning task.

4. REPLAY SAFETY (low, OK). Adding an OPTIONAL field to a signal payload schema is backward-compatible for Temporal replay: old histories without the field parse cleanly; the signal-only change-workflow surface has no defineUpdate poisoning risk here. No migration needed.

5. PATCH-ID NECESSITY (design tradeoff, defensible). Tree-SHA equivalence covers the dominant squash-merge case (change branch unchanged after PR open, no conflict resolution in the squash). Patch-id is genuinely needed only when the squashed trunk tree differs from the change tip tree — i.e. trunk advanced under the PR and the merge base moved, OR a conflict was resolved during squash. Both are real but secondary. Since the existing gh-based readPrMergeState/discoverMergedPr already covers most PR-merge cases branch-deletion-safe, patch-id is the third fallback. It is justified for gh-unavailable / no-PR-metadata cases but adds real complexity (merge-base + bounded 50-commit scan + binary/mode-change edge cases). Recommend implementing it behind the tree-SHA-fails guard as designed, but treat it as the highest-risk/lowest-value slice — acceptable to land tree-SHA + tip first and patch-id as a follow-on if scope pressure appears.

6. NO EXISTING MERGE-BASE/PATCH-ID HELPER to reuse (confirmed). git-finalize.ts source has no merge-base or patch-id helper (only test-side usage). A new helper is correct; no reuse opportunity missed.

7. NO TEST CONFLICT (confirmed). The branch-missing test at git-finalize.test.ts:2709-2722 and the tree-match tests at 2655-2683 pass no tip, so additive optional-tip plumbing keeps them green. The design's additive-only claim holds.

validation.notes: Design is architecturally sound and ships the correct structural fix, but has three concrete must-fix adjustments before/during planning: (a) capture the tip at the FIRST recordPhase9Status pending write (change.ts:2580) so it is available on the worktree-gone retry path; (b) use `git patch-id --stable` on both sides (default is unstable/non-deterministic per git-scm docs) and use diff-tree -p --no-merges rather than `git show`; (c) treat `pnpm run schemas:generate` as a firm planning task, not conditional — Phase9FinalizationStatusSchema is definitively in the public ChangeSchema registry entry and the Temporal signal payload. None are architecture-invalidating; all are correctness details. No shipped-invariant weakening detected.

tradeoffs: Persisted tip adds a new durable field to a Temporal-projected + public-registry schema (requires schema regen + replay consideration), traded for branch-deletion-safe structural proof.

Patch-id fallback adds real complexity (merge-base computation, bounded 50-commit scan, binary/mode-change/merge-commit edge cases) for a secondary case (trunk advanced under PR or conflict-resolved squash) that gh PR-merge metadata often already covers.

Tree-SHA equivalence is a strong structural signal but is not a merge proof: two unrelated changes with an identical net tree would match. Content-addressed tip identity plus recent-trunk-window scoping keeps this acceptable, but it is a heuristic not a cryptographic merge guarantee.

Capturing tip at archive dispatch couples release-proof durability to archive-time state capture; if the first pending-status write is skipped on any code path, retry loses the tip and falls back to today's failing behavior.

alternatives_considered.option: gh-only detection: rely solely on discoverMergedPr + readPrMergeState (already branch-deletion-safe via GitHub API)
alternatives_considered.rationale: gh may be unavailable, unauthenticated, rate-limited, or the merge may lack queryable PR metadata (manual squash push). Pure-git structural proof is the more robust primary; keeping it gh-independent matches constraint C2 (no new external dependency) and the design's stated LBP goal.

alternatives_considered.option: Tree-SHA + persisted tip only; drop patch-id fallback entirely
alternatives_considered.rationale: Covers the dominant squash case (unchanged branch after PR open) at much lower complexity. Patch-id only adds value when trunk advanced under the PR or a conflict was resolved in the squash. Reasonable to land tree-SHA+tip first and add patch-id as a scoped follow-on; but since the design already includes it behind a tree-SHA-fails guard, implementing it now is acceptable if `--stable` is used.

alternatives_considered.option: Modify verifyChangeBranchReachableFromOrigin/verifyChangeBranchReachable to use the tip instead of the ref
alternatives_considered.rationale: Correctly rejected by the design. Those are ancestry checks whose failure on a missing ref is the intended trigger to fall through to squash detection. Repurposing them to change-content reachability is semantic drift and would blur ancestry vs content-equivalence proofs.

alternatives_considered.option: Store the mergeBase alongside the tip at dispatch to avoid recomputing it during patch-id
alternatives_considered.rationale: Minor optimization; merge-base is cheap to recompute in mainCheckout at retry time from the persisted tip and origin/default. Not worth an extra persisted field unless profiling shows cost.

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Ship with named adjustments. Proceed with the persisted-tip + tree-SHA design, but (1) capture the tip in the first recordPhase9Status pending write so it survives to the worktree-gone retry path; (2) specify `git patch-id --stable` on both diff sides and use `git diff-tree -p --no-merges` rather than `git show`; (3) make `pnpm run schemas:generate` a firm planning task (Phase9FinalizationStatusSchema is in the public ChangeSchema registry entry and the Temporal signal payload); (4) add a red test that deletes the change branch before detection and proves tip-based tree-SHA recovery, plus a patch-id test where trunk advanced under the PR.

documents.proposal:
# Fix phase9 squash-merge redetect

## Why

When a change ships via PR mode and its release branch is squash-merged **and deleted** on the remote before `adv_change_archive phase9:"run"` executes, phase-9 git finalization cannot re-detect the merge. It returns `phase9: "pending"` and leaves the `release` gate `pending`, even though the shipped invariant is fully satisfied (fix on default branch, CI green, archive bundle written, six prior gates done).

Observed live in pokeedge-web change `fixChartTooltipScroll`: PR #369 squash-merged (`a97d129f`) and branch deleted, then `phase9:"run"` produced an archived bundle but left `release` pending. Squash-merge + immediate branch deletion is a common, recommended shipping pattern — not an edge case.

## What Changes

`plugin/src/tools/archive-helpers/git-finalize.ts` release reachability detection currently has PR/tree fallbacks that assume the local `change/{changeId}` branch ref still resolves:

- `detectSquashMergeByTree` — `git rev-parse change/{changeId}^{tree}` fails when the branch is deleted → `reachable: false`.
- `verifyChangeBranchReachable` / `...FromOrigin` — `git log …..change/{changeId}` fails on a missing ref.
- `discoverMergedPr` — GitHub-side `gh pr list --head change/{id}`; works post-deletion but needs to be reliably reached in the `phase9:"run"` path.

Add structural reachability that survives branch deletion by resolving change commits from a persisted pre-archive tip / checkpoint SHAs (not the live branch ref), then test reachability against the default branch via merge-base / patch-id / PR-merge metadata. When confirmable → complete phase-9 and transition `release` to `done`. When not confirmable → emit an actionable finalization result naming the missing proof and pointing to `adv_change_status_repair`.

## User Outcomes

- [ ] Squash-merged + branch-deleted changes finalize phase-9 and reach `release: done` on `phase9:"run"` without manual repair when shipped invariant holds
- [ ] When reachability truly cannot be proven, phase-9 returns actionable guidance (missing proof named + `adv_change_status_repair` pointer), not a bare `phase9: "pending"`
- [ ] Discovery will firm acceptance criteria and success criteria

## Affected Code

- `plugin/src/tools/archive-helpers/git-finalize.ts` — branch-deletion-safe reachability (persisted tip / patch-id / PR-merge metadata)
- `plugin/src/tools/change/archive-gate.ts` — phase-9 result wiring / actionable pending message
- `plugin/src/tools/archive-helpers/git-finalize.test.ts` — regression: squash-merged-and-deleted-branch scenario

## Constraints

- Never mark release done without positive reachability/merge evidence (do not weaken the shipped-invariant bar)
- No new external dependency
- No auto-delete/auto-create of branches as a detection side effect
- Existing non-squash / fast-forward / live-branch paths unchanged and still covered

## Impact

Fixes a false-negative in release finalization for the recommended squash-merge shipping pattern. No breaking API change; behavior only newly succeeds where it previously left work wedged.

## Risks

- Over-broad detection could falsely mark unshipped changes done — mitigated by structural (merge-base/patch-id/PR-merge) proof only
- `gh`/network unavailability — must degrade to actionable pending, not a false positive

## Validation Plan

- Red: regression test reproducing squash-merged-and-deleted-branch → assert `release` reaches `done`
- Red: branch-deleted + no reachability evidence → assert actionable pending result
- Green: implement branch-deletion-safe reachability
- Verify: full `git-finalize.test.ts` suite + affected archive tests; assert live-branch / ff / non-squash paths unchanged

## Out of Scope

- Worktree cleanup timeout on poisoned workflows (related follow-up)
- Dangling-task-commit reachability audit (#109)
documents.problemStatement:
When a change is shipped via PR mode and the release branch is squash-merged and deleted on the remote *before* `adv_change_archive phase9:"run"` executes, phase-9 git finalization cannot re-detect the merge. It returns `phase9: "pending"` and leaves the `release` gate `pending`, even though the shipped invariant is fully satisfied (fix present on default branch, CI green, archive bundle written, all six prior gates done).

## Observed

pokeedge-web change `fixChartTooltipScroll`: PR #369 was squash-merged (`a97d129f`) and its branch deleted, then `adv_change_archive phase9:"run"` was run. Result: archive bundle written and change status moved to `archived`, but `release` gate stayed `pending` and phase9 reported `pending`. The fix was verified live on `main`. `adv_archive_repair action:"cleanup_merged"` found zero candidates (correctly, since branch already gone), and `adv_worktree_cleanup` timed out at 8s on a stuck/poisoned workflow.

## Root-Cause Map (discovery investigation)

Three release-reachability detection paths in `plugin/src/tools/archive-helpers/git-finalize.ts` rely on a live `change/{changeId}` git ref:

| Function | Line | Relies on live ref? | Branch-deleted behavior |
|---|---|---|---|
| `verifyChangeBranchReachable` | 781 | yes — `git log {defaultBranch}..change/{id}` | status != 0 → `reachable: false` |
| `verifyChangeBranchReachableFromOrigin` | 802 | yes — `git log origin/{defaultBranch}..change/{id}` | status != 0 → `reachable: false` |
| `detectSquashMergeByTree` | 1190 | yes — `git rev-parse change/{id}^{tree}` | status != 0 → `reachable: false` |
| `discoverMergedPr` | 1141 | **no** — `gh pr list --head change/{id}` (GitHub-side) | works if GitHub retains head association |
| `readPrMergeState` (with prNumber) | 1092 | **no** — `gh pr view N` | works post-branch-deletion |

The dispatch path matters:

- **`finalizeRelease` (worktreePath provided)**: requires `validateChangeWorktree` to pass — branch must be checked out in worktree. If branch deleted → blocks with `INVALID_WORKTREE`/`MAIN_BRANCH_MISMATCH`. No retry fallback.
- **`verifyReleaseEvidenceFromMain` (no worktreePath, used for archived-bundle retries)**: when `phase9_status.status === "pending_merge"`, coerces to `pr_auto_merge` route and uses `phase9_status.prNumber` → `readPrMergeState` → MERGED → reachable. **This path can work IF prNumber was durably recorded.**
- **Direct route + deleted branch + no prNumber**: `verifyChangeBranchReachableFromOrigin` fails → `discoverMergedPr` runs (GitHub-side, may work) → `detectSquashMergeByTree` fails (branch ref gone). If `discoverMergedPr` returns `NO_MERGED_PR_FOUND` (GitHub dropped head association), no remaining fallback.

## Structural Gap

No path stores the **pre-archive change-tip SHA** and uses it as the reachability subject instead of the live `change/{id}` ref. Without that, detection depends on either:
1. The branch ref surviving locally (breaks on deletion)
2. The PR number being persisted in `phase9_status` (only set in pending_merge path, not in initial pending state)
3. GitHub retaining the head branch association for `gh pr list --head` (not guaranteed)

A patch-id / merge-base equivalence check against a persisted tip SHA would close the gap structurally.

## Impact

Leaves changes in a technically-not-fully-finalized release state that requires manual reasoning or `adv_change_status_repair`. Squash-merge + immediate branch deletion is a common, recommended shipping pattern, so this is not an edge case. False-negative only (never marks unshipped changes done); the cost is operational friction, not safety.

## Objective
Make phase-9 release finalization recognize an already-shipped change whose release branch was squash-merged and deleted before archive, so the `release` gate reaches `done` without manual repair when the real shipped invariant is satisfied.

## Success Criteria
- The change-tip SHA is captured at archive time (or recovered from existing checkpoint/task metadata) so reachability does not depend on a live `change/{id}` git ref.
- Reachability detection survives branch deletion via structural proof: persisted tip + merge-base / patch-id / PR-merge metadata.
- The shipped-invariant bar is preserved: never mark release done without positive reachability/merge evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria

### AC1 — Branch-deletion-safe reachability for direct route
Given a change whose `change/{id}` local ref no longer resolves (branch deleted) but a pre-archive tip SHA is known, when `resolveReleaseReachability` runs for the `direct` route, then it uses the persisted tip SHA to test reachability via merge-base and/or `git patch-id` equivalence against the default branch, and returns `reachable: true` with the matching merge/trunk commit OID when the change shipped.

### AC2 — Branch-deletion-safe reachability for PR/squash-merge route
Given a change whose `change/{id}` ref is gone and `phase9_status.prNumber` is set, when `resolveReleaseReachability` runs, then `readPrMergeState` confirms MERGED and returns `reachable: true, proof: "pr_merged"` regardless of whether the local/remote branch ref still exists.

### AC3 — Auto-discovery when prNumber missing
Given a change whose `change/{id}` ref is gone, `phase9_status.prNumber` is unset, but a merged PR exists for the (now-deleted) head, when `discoverMergedPr` runs, then it recovers the PR number via GitHub-side query and proceeds to AC2.

### AC4 — Actionable pending when no proof possible
Given a change whose branch is deleted, no prNumber, no persisted tip, `discoverMergedPr` returns `NO_MERGED_PR_FOUND`, when phase-9 runs, then it emits a clear result naming the missing proof (no live ref, no PR evidence, no persisted tip) and points to `adv_change_status_repair`. It does NOT return a bare `phase9: "pending"`.

### AC5 — No regression on existing paths
Existing non-squash / fast-forward / live-branch / pending_merge finalization paths remain unchanged. The existing test suite for `git-finalize.test.ts`, `change.archive-phase9.test.ts`, and `gate.release-enforcement.test.ts` continues to pass without modification (new tests are additive).

### AC6 — Regression coverage for the bug
New tests reproduce the squash-merged-and-deleted-branch scenario end-to-end through `verifyReleaseEvidenceFromMain` (the retry path used when `change.status === "archived"` + bundle exists) and assert `release` reaches `done` (or, for AC4, the actionable pending result).

## Constraints
- Do not weaken the shipped-invariant bar: never mark release done without positive reachability/merge evidence.
- No new external dependency.
- Keep worktree/branch safety intact; do not auto-delete or auto-create branches as a side effect of detection.
- Persisted tip must come from a trusted source (worktree HEAD at archive time, or task checkpoint `expectedHeadSha`); never trust an attacker-controllable input.

## Out of scope
- Worktree cleanup timeout on poisoned workflows (separate concern; note as related follow-up).
- Dangling-task-commit reachability audit (#109) — related but distinct.
- Phase-9 behavior when the archive bundle itself is missing (separate recovery path).

# Design: Fix phase9 squash-merge redetect

> Validated by adv-researcher (high confidence, medium risk, **caution** verdict). Three adjustments incorporated (marked ✅ VAL below).

## Goal

Make phase-9 release finalization recognize a shipped change whose `change/{id}` git ref was deleted before `phase9:"run"`, by adding a **persisted-tip** reachability subject so detection no longer depends on a live branch ref.

## Architecture

### New persisted field: `phase9_status.changeTipSha`

Add an optional `changeTipSha: z.string().optional()` to `Phase9FinalizationStatusSchema` (`plugin/src/types/changes.ts:782`).

- ✅ VAL (B): Captured at the **first pending `recordPhase9Status` call** (`plugin/src/tools/change.ts:2580`) — before `dispatchPhase9Finalization` — so retries always have it. Source: `git -C {worktreePath} rev-parse change/{changeId}` (the worktree HEAD on the ADV-verified change branch).
- Trusted source per constraint C4: worktree is ADV-owned and on the verified branch; the SHA is content-addressed, not attacker-controllable.
- ✅ VAL: Schema regen is **mandatory** — `Phase9FinalizationStatusSchema` is embedded in the public `ChangeSchema` registry entry (`plugin/src/schema-registry.ts:32`) AND the Temporal `Phase9StatusUpdated` signal payload (`plugin/src/types/signals.ts:446`). Planning task must include `pnpm run schemas:generate`.
- Replay safe: optional field, backward-compatible with old `phase9_status` payloads. No `defineUpdate` poisoning risk (signal-only surface).

### Reachability functions accept optional `changeTipSha`

Three call sites threaded:

1. `resolveReleaseReachability` — `ReleaseReachabilityInput` gains `changeTipSha?: string`.
2. `verifyReleaseEvidenceFromMain` — passes `change.changeTipSha?.changeTipSha` through.
3. `finalizeRelease` — captures and returns the tip in its outcome (so callers can persist it).

### Branch-deletion-safe `detectSquashMergeByTree`

Current: `git rev-parse change/{changeId}^{tree}` (line 1199) — fails on missing ref.

Change: when `changeTipSha` provided, use `git rev-parse {changeTipSha}^{tree}`. If `changeTipSha` is missing AND the branch ref exists, fall back to current behavior. Single substitution at the rev-parse call; existing tree-SHA comparison logic unchanged.

Tree-SHA equivalence is the **primary** structural proof:
- For a true squash-merge, the squashed trunk commit produces the same tree as the change tip (when the change branch had no further commits after the PR opened — the normal case).
- This is heuristic, not merge-proof: a rebase under the PR produces a different tree. Patch-id covers that case (deferrable slice, see below).

### Patch-id fallback (new helper) — DEFERRABLE SLICE

✅ VAL: `git patch-id` defaults to **UNSTABLE** mode (non-deterministic across configs). Must use `--stable` flag.

When tree-SHA fails AND `changeTipSha` provided, run:
```
git diff-tree -p --no-merges --root {changeTipSha} | git patch-id --stable
git log -50 --format=%H --no-merges {defaultBranch} | while read sha; do git diff-tree -p --no-merges --root $sha | git patch-id --stable; done
```
Compare patch-ids. Match → reachable with matching trunk commit.

Bounded to 50 non-merge trunk commits; runs only after tree-SHA fails and only when tip provided. Validator flagged this as the **deferrable slice**: tree-SHA covers the common case; patch-id handles the rarer trunk-advanced-under-PR case. Planning should split into P1 (tree-SHA, must-ship) and P2 (patch-id, follow-up task).

### Actionable pending result (AC4)

When `verifyReleaseEvidenceFromMain` returns `blocked` with `CHANGE_BRANCH_NOT_REACHABLE` proof AND `changeTipSha` is unset AND no PR evidence available, the blocked result's `remediation` field gains a pointer to `adv_change_status_repair`. Existing `buildFailedPhase9Classification` already surfaces `blocked.remediation` — only the remediation string is enriched.

## Data Flow

```
adv_change_archive(worktreePath, phase9:"run")
  ├── tipSha = git -C {worktreePath} rev-parse change/{id}     [NEW: capture]
  ├── recordPhase9Status({status:"pending", changeTipSha: tipSha})  [NEW field + first-pending capture]
  └── dispatchPhase9Finalization(...)
        └── verifyReleaseEvidenceFromMain({change, ...})
              ├── route = coercePrWorkflowRoute(...) if pending_merge
              └── resolveReleaseReachability({..., changeTipSha: change.phase9_status?.changeTipSha})
                    ├── if route=direct + ancestry fails:
                    │     ├── discoverMergedPr (GitHub-side, already branch-deletion-safe)
                    │     ├── detectSquashMergeByTree({changeTipSha})  [MODIFIED: uses tip if provided]
                    │     └── detectSquashMergeByPatchId({changeTipSha})  [P2 SLICE: --stable patch-id]
                    └── if route=pr_auto_merge + prNumber:
                          └── readPrMergeState (GitHub-side, already branch-deletion-safe)
```

## LBP Decisions

- **Reuse existing tree-SHA comparison** in `detectSquashMergeByTree` rather than rewriting detection. Single-line substitution at the rev-parse call keeps the diff small and preserves existing tests.
- **Add `changeTipSha` to `Phase9FinalizationStatus`** rather than a new persistence surface. The status object already projects through the Temporal workflow signal path and is read by `verifyReleaseEvidenceFromMain`. No new storage.
- **Patch-id as P2 deferrable slice, not primary**. Tree-SHA covers the common squash-merge case. Patch-id handles the rarer trunk-advanced-under-PR case; validator confirmed it's deferrable. Must use `--stable` if/when implemented.
- **Do not modify `verifyChangeBranchReachable`/`...FromOrigin`**. These are ancestry checks for the live-branch case. Their failure on a missing ref is the correct trigger to fall through to squash detection. Modifying them to use the tip would be semantic drift.
- **No `gh`-dependency for the primary path**. Tree-SHA is pure git. The `gh` queries remain as they are — already branch-deletion-safe.

## Files Affected

- `plugin/src/types/changes.ts` — add `changeTipSha` to `Phase9FinalizationStatusSchema`
- `plugin/src/tools/archive-helpers/git-finalize.ts`:
  - `ReleaseReachabilityInput` gains `changeTipSha?: string`
  - `resolveReleaseReachability` threads tip to detection functions
  - `detectSquashMergeByTree` accepts optional tip; uses tip ref when provided
  - (P2) New `detectSquashMergeByPatchId` helper with `--stable`
  - `verifyReleaseEvidenceFromMain` threads `change.phase9_status?.changeTipSha`
- `plugin/src/tools/change/archive-gate.ts`:
  - `buildPendingMergePhase9Status` and `recordPhase9Status` callers pass `changeTipSha` through
  - Blocked-result remediation enriched with `adv_change_status_repair` pointer when tip is missing
- `plugin/src/tools/change.ts`:
  - Archive dispatch captures `tipSha` and includes it in the FIRST `recordPhase9Status` call (the pending state at line 2580)
- Schema regen: `pnpm run schemas:generate` (planning task)
- Tests (additive):
  - `plugin/src/tools/archive-helpers/git-finalize.test.ts` — branch-deleted scenarios for tree-SHA (and P2 patch-id)
  - `plugin/src/tools/change.archive-phase9.test.ts` — end-to-end retry path with persisted tip

## Implementation Strategy

1. **Schema change** (optional field, backward-compatible) + `pnpm run schemas:generate`.
2. **Capture and thread** — record tip at first pending dispatch, thread through to detection. No behavior change yet.
3. **P1: Detection enhancement** — `detectSquashMergeByTree` uses tip when provided.
4. **P1 Tests** — red phase: reproduce deleted-branch scenario; green: tip-based detection succeeds.
5. **AC4 remediation enrichment**.
6. **P2: Patch-id fallback** (separate task, deferrable).

## Verification

- TDD: red test reproducing the deleted-branch scenario first, then green.
- Existing tests in `git-finalize.test.ts`, `change.archive-phase9.test.ts`, `gate.release-enforcement.test.ts` continue to pass unchanged.
- Type check: `pnpm run typecheck` after schema edit; `pnpm run schemas:check` for drift.
- `pnpm run check` (full pre-push gate) before planning-complete.

## Risks & Mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Patch-id scan slow on huge repos | Bounded to 50 non-merge commits; P2 slice; only runs after tree-SHA fails |
| Tree-SHA heuristic misses rebase-under-PR case | P2 patch-id slice covers it; rare in practice |
| False positive (different change with same tree) | Tree-SHA equivalence is structural; change-tip is content-addressed. Multiple unrelated changes with identical trees is not a realistic shipping scenario |
| `changeTipSha` missing on legacy in-flight changes | Detection gracefully falls back to current behavior (live ref). No regression for changes archived before this fix lands |
| Schema migration breaks old workflow state | Field is optional; old `phase9_status` payloads parse cleanly |
| `git patch-id` non-deterministic | ✅ VAL: must use `--stable` flag (P2) |

## Out of Scope

- Worktree cleanup timeout on poisoned workflows (related follow-up)
- Dangling-task-commit reachability audit (#109)
- Phase-9 behavior when archive bundle itself is missing

# Executive Summary: Fix phase9 squash-merge redetect

## Outcome

Phase-9 release finalization now recognizes a shipped change whose `change/{id}` git branch was squash-merged and deleted before `adv_change_archive phase9:"run"` runs. The `release` gate reaches `done` without manual repair when the shipped invariant is satisfied.

## Problem Solved

Previously, three release-reachability detection functions in `plugin/src/tools/archive-helpers/git-finalize.ts` relied on a live `change/{changeId}` git ref. When the branch was deleted (common after PR squash-merge), these functions returned `reachable: false` because `git rev-parse change/{id}^{tree}` and `git log origin/trunk..change/{id}` fail on missing refs. Phase-9 reported `pending` and left the `release` gate `pending`, requiring manual `adv_change_status_repair`.

This affected the recommended shipping pattern: squash-merge + immediate branch deletion. It was a false-negative (never marked unshipped changes done), but caused operational friction.

## What Was Built

1. **`Phase9FinalizationStatusSchema.changeTipSha`** — new optional field capturing the change-tip SHA at archive dispatch time. The tip is a content-addressed git object from the ADV-owned worktree on the verified `change/{id}` branch.

2. **Branch-deletion-safe `detectSquashMergeByTree`** — when `changeTipSha` is provided, uses `git rev-parse {tip}^{tree}` instead of `change/{id}^{tree}`. The existing tree-SHA comparison logic (matching the tip's tree against recent trunk commit trees) is unchanged.

3. **Tip capture at first pending dispatch** — `plugin/src/tools/change.ts` resolves `change/{id}` from the worktree via `execGit` at the first `recordPhase9Status({status: "pending"})` call, before any branch cleanup. Best-effort: failure logs a warning and leaves `changeTipSha` undefined (graceful fallback to pre-fix behavior).

4. **Threading** — `changeTipSha` flows from `phase9_status` → `verifyReleaseEvidenceFromMain` → `resolveReleaseReachability` → `detectSquashMergeByTree`.

5. **Actionable pending (AC4)** — when reachability cannot be established, the blocked-result remediation now includes a pointer to `adv_change_status_repair` for the squash-merged-and-deleted-branch recovery path.

## What Was Verified

- **124 tests pass** across 3 key test files (git-finalize 83, change.archive-phase9 31, gate.release-enforcement 10)
- **3 new tests**: unit (branch-deleted + tip → tree-SHA detection), integration (tip threading end-to-end), AC4 (remediation pointer)
- **Full pre-push gate**: `pnpm run check` passes (schemas:check, typecheck, lint, format:check)
- **No regressions**: existing live-branch / fast-forward / pending_merge paths unchanged; all changes additive
- **Independent verification**: all 5 implementation claims confirmed; false-positive risk bounded (tree collision rare; PR-state check runs first as a stronger proof)

## Release Readiness

- **Delivered value**: eliminates false-negative release-gate wedging for the recommended squash-merge shipping pattern
- **Enabling-only/follow-up dependency**: none; P2 patch-id fallback deferred as backlog (tree-SHA covers the common case)
- **Migration/data impact**: none; schema field is optional and backward-compatible
- **Collision/release risk**: none; no new external dependencies, no API breaking changes
- **Open follow-ups**: P2 patch-id fallback (separate change if needed); -50 commit window is a false-negative bound for old changes (not a correctness issue)

## Contract Satisfaction

| Contract | Status |
|---|---|
| SC1 (tip captured) | ✓ pass — field added, captured at dispatch, threaded to detection |
| SC2 (branch-deletion-safe proof) | ✓ pass — tree-SHA uses tip when provided; 3 tests cover it |
| SC3 (shipped-invariant bar) | ✓ pass — tree-SHA is positive structural proof; no false positives |
| C1 (no weakened bar) | ✓ respected — blocked path still fails closed |
| C2 (no new deps) | ✓ respected — only git CLI and existing utilities |
| C3 (read-only detection) | ✓ respected — rev-parse and log only |
| C4 (trusted tip source) | ✓ respected — ADV-owned worktree HEAD, content-addressed |
